source.title: Rigorously Assessing Natural Language Explanations of Neurons
source.authors: Jing Huang; Atticus Geiger; Karel D'Oosterlinck; Zhengxuan Wu; Christopher Potts

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses neuron-group interventions in GPT-2 XL to assess whether model behavior is carried by groups of neurons rather than individual neurons. This conceptually bears on distributed representations, but it does not test superposition geometry in toy models.
record.gate_note: The paper tests explanations of neurons and groups of semantically similar neurons, not superposition geometry, feature sparsity or importance, or an SAE dictionary. Its observational explanation-faithfulness scores are not included as rows because they do not directly measure whether features are distributed across neurons. The intervention results on group-level causal effects and the absence of a found single-neuron causal effect bear indirectly on V4.
record.test_reason: The study is about the faithfulness of GPT-4 neuron explanations, not superposition. Its interchange-intervention results in GPT-2 XL still bear on V4's 'features spread across many neurons'. Concept-level causal effects appear only with groups of tens to hundreds of neurons, and no single-neuron effect was found. This is indirect evidence: distributed causal mediation does not separate superposition from redundancy or multi-layer computation. No SAE or dictionary is used.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. GPT-4 explanations of GPT-2 XL neurons have low observational faithfulness (F1 about 0.56–0.60). They also have causal efficacy about equal to randomly chosen neurons, except for number neurons. The authors argue individual neurons are not the best unit of analysis and favour explaining groups of neurons with structured formalisms.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates natural-language neuron explanations using activation-based observational tests and causal interchange interventions; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Causal effects vary with the proportion and selection of neurons intervened on, and with layer location: IIA rises as K increases; middle and later layers show effects only after aggregation across consecutive layers.
record.peer_reviewed: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: Evidence is primarily from one pre-trained GPT-2 XL model. Intervention tasks and locations are curated rather than exhaustively searched; the authors note that exhaustive search over token positions was not performed. The extracted text gives intervention trends but not the numerical values plotted in the figures.
record.rows_left_out: The task-by-task IIA@K curves in Table 4 are figure-only in the provided text; their exact values are not recoverable. The text's aggregate findings are recorded in r2–r3. Observational F1, precision, and recall results concern faithfulness of neuron explanations, not feature distribution across neurons.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All of it: no capacity or importance manipulation.
All of it: the causes of polysemanticity are not studied.
SAE or dictionary recovery of sparse features. Whether the distributed causal effects reflect superposition specifically.
All of it: no SAE features.
All of it: feature dimensionality is not studied.

missing.what: Observational probe F1 rises with more semantically similar neurons: GPT-4 explanations 0.56 (N=1) to 0.73 (N=16). The random-neuron baseline rises too (0.00 to 0.69). This bears weakly on concepts being spread across neurons.
Manual inspection of 100 explanations with Type II errors. Most errors are neurons firing on unrelated but coherent concepts, a polysemanticity observation. At least 6 cases involve antonyms.

record.verdict_notes: The superposition relevance is secondary to the paper's aim. Results are one model, curated tasks and hand-chosen intervention positions, with no uncertainty reported and IIA values shown only in figures. The reader's limits_scope label is dropped because r3 and r4 are consistent with V4, not qualifications of it.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether it is insufficient evidence for superposition.
The study reports neuron-group effects in GPT-2 XL, but does not test SAE-recovered features or their sparsity.
SAE feature completeness, stability, and canonical status.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.operation_detail: Interchange interventions on the top 20% of first-layer neurons selected by token-activation correlation.
rows.measure: Share of causal effect, reported as IIA
rows.note: The authors state that a relatively small subset of first-layer neurons accounts for this effect, while the granularity remains hundreds of neurons.
rows.check: The baseline is the random-selection baseline and IIA@100, not 'not stated'. The 80% is relative to the whole-layer effect, using correlation-selected neurons in layer 0. The authors stress the unit is still hundreds of neurons.

source_check.correct: First-layer correlation-selected top 20% of neurons account for 80% of the whole-layer causal effect. The reference is whole-layer intervention (IIA@100); random neuron selection is also an experimental baseline. The 80% is a share of causal effect, not a reported absolute IIA of 80%.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 4.2–4.4; Table 4 caption; Section 4.4 paragraph on first-layer correlation-selected neurons.
source_check.problem: The baseline field omits the whole-layer reference and random-selection control.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.operation_detail: Interchange interventions using the MLP-layer neurons as a whole.
rows.measure: Interchange intervention accuracy (IIA), causal effect on task behavior
rows.value: MLP-layer neurons show causal effects on all tasks
rows.note: The paper reports this as an aggregate across the evaluated tasks; numerical IIA values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Patching a whole MLP layer (K=100%) showing causal effects says nothing about whether a feature is spread across neurons. Patching the full layer naturally carries the information, so the row cannot show V4's effect.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.operation_detail: Interchange interventions across multiple consecutive MLP layers.
rows.value: Causal effects appear only after aggregating over multiple consecutive layers
rows.note: The result qualifies where aggregation is needed; the paper does not provide numerical values in the text.
rows.check: The state is relative to V4, not to the effect size. Needing to aggregate over several consecutive layers is consistent with distributed storage, so the row is observed rather than partial. Values are figure-only.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.4, discussion of middle and later layers; Table 4.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.measure: Whether an intervention changes model behavior causally
rows.value: The authors report that they did not find a task where intervening on a single neuron changed model behavior causally
rows.note: This is a reported search outcome, not a claim that every possible single-neuron intervention was exhaustively tested.
rows.check: The single-neuron effect is absent, but that is what V4 predicts, so the state for V4 is observed. It is a stated search outcome, not a measured value. The smallest tested K=1% is already many neurons, so single neurons were not systematically swept.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.4, final sentences discussing intervention granularity.

relationships.display_finding: Interventions had causal effects only with groups of hundreds of neurons or several layers, and no single-neuron effect was found. This is indirect evidence for distributed representations, not specifically for superposition.

relation.reason: Its own neuron-group and multilayer interventions bear on V4's distributed-feature claim, despite explanation faithfulness being the primary research question.

tranche.reason: The explanation-faithfulness study reports causal results bearing on distributed representations in pretrained GPT-2 XL, a new setting relative to the original toy-model work.

source_check.notes: The single-neuron result is a reported search outcome, not an exhaustive impossibility claim; Table 4's smallest reported selection is 1% of neurons. The text describes granularity of hundreds of neurons; these findings do not establish capacity-driven superposition.
